question.problem:
The function $f(x)$ is defined for every real number $x$ and is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}6k-20{x}^{2}, & x\ne 1, \\ -8, & x=1.\end{aligned}
$$

If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1,$ what is the value of $k?$

$k=$ 
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$

$$
{lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)={lim}_{x\to 1}(6k-20{x}^{2})=6k-20.
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=1,$ we must have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}f(x) & =f(1) \\ 6k-20 & =-8 \\ 6k & =12 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting $k=2$ removes the point discontinuity.
